text:
Predicates:
MountainRange(x) ::: x is a mountain range.
LocatedIn(x, y) ::: x is located in y.
Visited(x, y) ::: x visited y.
Donated(x) ::: x was donated.
HasMine(x, y) ::: x has a mine y.
Mine(y) ::: y is a mine.
Texas(x) ::: x is Texas.
NewMexico(x) ::: x is New Mexico.
PicurisMountains ::: the Picuris Mountains.
JuanDeOnate ::: Juan de Onate.
HardingPegmatiteMine ::: the Harding Pegmatite Mine.

Premises:
(MountainRange(PicurisMountains) ∧ (LocatedIn(PicurisMountains, NewMexico) ∨ LocatedIn(PicurisMountains, Texas))) ::: The Picuris Mountains are a mountain range in New Mexico or Texas.
Visited(JuanDeOnate, PicurisMountains) ::: Juan de Onate visited the Picuris Mountains.
(HasMine(PicurisMountains, HardingPegmatiteMine) ∧ Donated(HardingPegmatiteMine)) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine, located in the Picuris Mountains, was donated.
¬∃x (MountainRange(x) ∧ LocatedIn(x, Texas) ∧ ∃y (Mine(y) ∧ HasMine(x, y) ∧ Donated(y))) ::: There are no mountain ranges in Texas that have mines which have been donated.

Conclusion:
Visited(JuanDeOnate, x) ∧ MountainRange(x) ∧ LocatedIn(x, NewMexico) ::: Juan de Onate visited a mountain range in New Mexico.
